answer: Imagine the agent economy as an ocean crossed by a limited number of voyages each epoch, each voyage a scarce, high-value data lane. Access is sold in a sealed-bid auction, and every identity must pay its own winning bid from its own balance, so no single wallet may fund two bids. A sybil operator's clones then bid against each other, driving up the price they pay themselves, while an honest agent bids once and sails. The lane is basalt-solid: a clone that wins but cannot do the work forfeits its bid to a public fraud bounty, so duplication becomes a tax the attacker levies on itself.
